the AMPT model reproduces the measured anisotropic flow data for Au + Au collisions at RHIC energies.
the AMPT model is able to describe the rapidity and the system size dependence of the anisotropic flow at RHIC, and the results are consistent with the available data.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the anisotropic flows at different rapidities in the same system size and the same anisotropic flows for different system sizes at the same rapidity are both insensitive to the initial conditions and are dominated by the final-state effects.
the anisotropic flows of the charged hadrons are sensitive to the system size, and the sensitivity of anisotropic flow to the system size is more pronounced at lower rapidities.
the rapidity dependence of anisotropy flow coefficients v(n) is weak, while the system size dependence is significant.
